messages:
Sam: Thanks everyone for joining the Q&A — quick clarification on the credits/quotas section from today?
Leah: Happy to take this. Which part felt unclear — burst behavior or the new per-route units?
Carlos: The burst pool rules — does unused burst carry over between billing periods?
Frank: Short answer: no carryover. Credits are monthly and we don’t roll unused burst forward.
Mira: Can you confirm how the burst pool gets refilled if you hit it twice in a month? Is there a cooldown?
Frank: No cooldown. It replenishes at the start of the next billing cycle. Within-cycle you can still request burst but subject to dynamic rate caps if system-wide pressure is high.
DevX Jen: For developer experience — is there an API to query remaining credits + burst usage in realtime?
Leah: Yes — we’re adding a /v1/usage balance endpoint in the next sprint. Beta docs due by EOD Friday.
Sam: @Leah, will that endpoint show committed Dedicated reservations separately from Hosted credits? Customers need to reconcile both.
Leah: Good call. We’ll return a breakdown: hosted credits, reserved/dedicated commitments, and transient burst consumed.
Carlos: About rate caps — you mentioned a soft per-minute cap and a hard emergency cap. How do retries get treated? Are they counted the same?
Frank: Retries count toward the same token units. We recommend exponential backoff. We will add guidance soon: retries that repeat the same request will be billed; idempotent retries are advised.
Mira: Any plan to expose per-route quotas in the Console so product teams can set internal guardrails?
Leah: Yes. Console v2 will let org admins set per-route soft quotas with alerting and auto-fallback rules. ETA Q3.
DevX Jen: Can we get sample policies — like JSON snippets for the fallback routing and quota thresholds for canaries?
Leah: I’ll drop examples in the docs repo and link in #docs. Example: 
```
{ "route": "/chat", "soft_quota": 500000, "fallback": ["gpt-compat-quantized", "gpt-compat-emb"], "alert_to": "@ops" }
```
Carlos: That helps. One more — if a customer pins a model version and it’s unavailable, do we auto-fallback or block?
Sam: Our philosophy: prefer auto-fallback to keep customer apps up, but honor pinned-version SLA options for enterprise customers who opt in to strict behavior.
Mira: For strict pinned SLAs, will we offer a guarantee window for capacity?
Frank: Yes — Dedicated customers can purchase reserved capacity windows. We’ll publish the capacity SLAs and surge pricing for guaranteed slots.
DevX Jen: Anything for dev/test environments? Low-cost dev credits or extended grace for sandbox usage?
Leah: We’re introducing a dev bundle: small monthly credit pool, lower priority on capacity, and extended trial period. Details in the pricing doc next week.
Sam: Action items: @Leah create the /v1/usage spec + examples; @Frank add retry billing + surge pricing notes; @DevX Jen collect sample policy snippets and add to the docs PR.
ops-bot: Reminder: action items assigned. Leah -> /v1/usage spec (due 2026-04-01). Frank -> retry billing notes (due 2026-04-03). DevX Jen -> doc PR with snippets (due 2026-03-29).
Carlos: Thanks — that cleared up most of my questions.
Mira: Same. Appreciate the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
Sam: Awesome. If anyone still has edge cases (multi-org billing, marketplace credits) DM me and we’ll route to finance/product.
Leah: I’ll post a short FAQ in #all-hands with the key bullets and links.
Sam: End of thread — thanks all!
